To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) growing both the generator and the discriminator progressively allows us to produce high-resolution images of unprecedented quality (e.g., 1024^4) with high inception score; (2) a simple technique for increasing variation in GAN results is to add a noise injection layer at the beginning of the generator; and (3) a new training metric, FID, which measures the distance between feature distributions of real and generated samples, can be used as an alternative to the inception score.
(a) growing GANs is a promising new training methodology; (b) this methodology is especially useful for improving the quality and stability of generated images;

(i) growing GANs in resolution and variation is a promising training paradigm, and (ii) we have achieved a state of the art unsupervised image generation quality of 8.8 on CIFAR10 and 153.6 on CelebA.

improving the training and quality of GANs, and our results contain a number of points that we hope will prove useful for future research.
